summary: Iter 51 — Phase 7 behavioural pattern detection (backend + frontend). Added /app/backend/tests/test_patterns.py with 13 new pattern-detection tests covering cold-start floor, all 5 pattern kinds (top_frequency, preferred_time_of_day, mood_at_time, unused_soundscapes, extension_favorite), dominance/threshold negative cases, dismiss/clear idempotency, URL-encoded key path decoding, auth-gate on all 3 endpoints, and USER_PATTERNS+agent_chat integration. All 13 pass (13.7s). Frontend E2E verified via Playwright on the live preview URL: pattern-greeting-chip rendered with correct highest-priority message (mood_at_time), dismiss-X hides chip and persists to server, reload surfaces next-priority pattern (top_frequency 432 Hz with CTA), clicking Start there arms the frequency (NOW TUNING 528→432 Hz) and adds the key to dismissed. My Patterns section shows all 4 admin patterns with correct headings, occurrence counts, per-row Dismiss buttons; Clear all restores everything and empties dismissed list.
critical_code_review_comments: PatternGreetingChip: dismissal is fire-and-forget (no error toast if the POST fails). Fine as design since the chip is a hint, but log the failure at least for observability.

unused_soundscapes pattern shows 'count: 0' in the API payload — MyPatternsSection correctly hides the '0 occurrences' badge for that row (nice). Consider omitting the field entirely on the backend to make the intent explicit (nudge vs. observed pattern).

mood_at_time carries no CTA even though we know a favourite label — the label is often a frequency (e.g. '432 Hz'). Since we know the freq from the label pattern, backend could attach an arm_frequency cta so the user can act on the chip's highest-priority pattern too. Currently the top-priority chip is the only one without a Start-there button.
Dashboard.jsx still >2100 lines (flagged iter 49/50). No regression this phase.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — all chip + section flows verified end-to-end
